extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers / scientists (readers and contributors to the Philosophical Transactions; members of the Royal Society and observational researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Writing and reporting observational and experimental natural-philosophy studies (experimental metallurgy, anatomy, astronomy, microscopy, mechanical inventions) for a learned journal. Emphasises precise measurements, description of methods, comparison with prior tables/works, and explanation of probable causes and sources of error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide precise quantitative measurements
rubrics_metrics.description: Give exact weights, counts, angles, altitudes, and proportions for experimental and observational results (e.g., grains, ounces, degrees, time from noon).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the text include many specific measures (e.g., 'the piece of regulus weighing 124 grains', 'observed altitude ... was 18° 11′', 'the remaining antimony ... remained 19 grains of gold'). Such numerical detail allows calculation of proportions and direct comparison between trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for and discuss sources of experimental loss or error
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify probable mechanisms for material loss or measurement error (powdering, papers, sparks, firing, blast on cupels), and discuss their relative likelihood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author lists possibilities: 'Some loss of gold may happen on powdering the regulus in an iron mortar, as also by the papers necessarily used... the greatest loss was by small sparks... It is not improbable also, that some loss of gold may take place on the firing of the antimony...'. Reporters should enumerate and reason about possible artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat experiments and report consistency/variation
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform repeated melts/observations and report how results change with repetition (gains/losses, changing proportions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text compares successive meltings: 'in repeating the melting of the regulus with fresh antimony ... the regulus gains weight each time, but is in proportion less rich in gold.' Repeats reveal systematic trends and contradictions to other procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe materials, preparation, and apparatus used
rubrics_metrics.description: State what materials and preparatory steps were used (type/amount of antimony, regulus preparation, firing with nitre and tartar, cupel refining, microscopes, lenses, plates and figures), so others can understand or replicate the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The account specifies e.g. 'the remaining antimony being reduced to a regulus by firing with nitre and tartar, of each equal weight to itself, and that regulus exhaled on the cupel'. Mechanical inventions are described with referenced figures (pi. 12, fig. 4, fig. 5) and parts named/labelled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare observations to established tables, models, and prior works
rubrics_metrics.description: Contrast measured/observed values with existing astronomical tables, botanical/herbal authors, or prior experiments and note agreements or discrepancies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'These calculations commonly show a considerable difference from the real observed times. Particularly, the philolaic tables make Saturn 19′ farther advanced in longitude than he really is by observation.' Also botanical and literary comparisons (Gerard, Parkinson, L'Obelius) are cited when describing species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propose and evaluate alternative explanations; justify conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: When unexpected results occur, propose possible causes and use additional observations or prior practice to favour one explanation over others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author weighs hypotheses: 'It has been suspected, that some gold may be dissipated by the blast on the cupels... But this is not so probable; because gold has been melted several times ... without any loss.' Use prior practice or controlled variation to support inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide anatomical/structural description with functional interpretation and comparative context
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe morphology in detail (counts, relative sizes, tissue descriptions) and relate structure to function and interspecies differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Du Verney's description of nasal laminae: their number, folding, arterial/nerve supply, glands, and how these relate to smell; Leuwenhoek's microscopy compares pipes in human teeth to those in cow and haddock and notes variation in size/shape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report observational conditions and derive timing/coordinates
rubrics_metrics.description: Record observation time, local altitude, horizon bearings, and use these to compute astronomical time or positional data, explicitly showing derivations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bulliald's occultation observation records altitudes and derives astronomical times 'whence it follows that the astronomical time from noon was given equal to 7^ 20"' and compares to mean time. Include enough positional/temporal data to permit recalculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and report instrument quality and magnification when making microscopic observations
rubrics_metrics.description: State the quality/type of lenses or microscopes used, note improvements in observation due to better glass, and describe observable structures accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leuwenhoek notes using 'better glasses than the former' and how structures (pipes vs. globules) became apparent; report instrument improvements and how they change interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include labelled figures/plates and cross-reference them in the text for mechanical or complex apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide diagrams with figure/plate numbers and refer to them in the narrative to clarify mechanisms and parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanical inventions are described with references: 'Fig. 4, pi. 12, represents the inside of the machine...'; the description names parts (F G H, DF, AB, drum) and explains function relative to the drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide provenance, citations, and literature context
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention prior authors, translations, and previous notices of works or species, and indicate how the present finding relates to or corrects them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Book notices and species reports routinely cite authorities (Charras, Hobbs, L'Obelius, Mathiolus, Bauhinus, Gerard, Parkinson). Also note when an English writer omitted a native species; contextualize novelty versus known literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe exceptional or monstrous cases with comprehensive internal and external detail
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting rare clinical or natural anomalies (monstrous births, long-retained foetus, large hydropic ovaries), give full macroscopic description of parts, their disposition, measurements, and any internal findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The accounts detail heads, hearts, lungs, double spina dorsi, weights ('secundine ... weighing about 8 pounds'), and internal observations on discolouration, adhesions, and contents. Such completeness supports medical/anatomical interpretation.
